qa.overall_assessment: BA spec has 3 blocking issues: (1) AC5 directly contradicts AC6 on pane borders, (2) mobile compact day-selector is referenced but has zero DOM specification, (3) AC1 does not assert that the active-row highlight updates on day change. Two additional major gaps: AF-01 typography has no verifiable AC, and AC1 active-highlight re-render is asserted only as a prose hint not an AC. All BA evidence claims verified against source files — every line reference is accurate.

blocking_issues.title: AC5 contradicts AC6: pane-middle border-none vs border-top accent
blocking_issues.description: AC5 states: '.pane elements have no border property set (or border: none)'. AC6 states: 'the middle column pane has a visible 8px top accent in color #2383e2 (implemented as border-top: 8px solid var(--accent) or equivalent)'. M9 CSS spec also specifies '.pane-middle { border-top: 8px solid var(--accent) }'. A dev implementing AC5 literally would remove all borders from .pane-middle, breaking AC6. A dev implementing AC6 would leave border-top on .pane-middle, failing AC5. QA verification would produce contradictory results depending on which AC is tested first. The spec text is internally inconsistent at the AC level.
blocking_issues.evidence: AC5 text: 'Then .pane elements have no border property set (or border: none)'. AC6 text: 'Then the middle column pane has a visible 8px top accent... border-top: 8px solid var(--accent)'. M9 CSS snippet: '.pane { border: none; border-radius: 0; }' and '.pane-middle { background: var(--bg); border-top: 8px solid var(--accent); }' — these two rules together correctly implement intent but AC5 text does not reflect this nuance.
blocking_issues.proposed_fix: Replace AC5's first assertion with: '.pane-days and .pane-candidates have no border property; .pane-middle has no full-box border but retains border-top: 8px solid var(--accent)'. This aligns AC5 with AC6 and M9 without contradiction.

blocking_issues.title: Mobile compact day-selector has no DOM specification
blocking_issues.description: M7 states 'Days exposed as a compact sticky selector at top of the middle pane on mobile'. AC8 states 'day selection accessible as a compact sticky UI within the middle pane'. Technical Hints say 'add mobile day-select compact selector inside pane-middle header'. However the spec provides NO DOM structure for this element: no ID, no HTML snippet, no element type (select vs button list vs nav), no CSS class, no event wiring spec. The old #day-select is being removed (Edge Case 4 and AC11 mandate this). A dev implementing M7 has no spec to follow and will invent a structure inconsistent with what QA will verify for AC8. This is an unresolvable ambiguity — dev and QA will independently invent different solutions.
blocking_issues.evidence: M7 text: 'mobile.js pane registry in mobile.js updated...Days exposed as a compact sticky selector at top of the middle pane on mobile'. AC8 THEN clause: 'day selection accessible as a compact sticky UI within the middle pane'. No HTML snippet for the mobile day selector is provided anywhere in the spec. The HTML structure snippet in Technical Hints shows #pane-middle with a .middle-tab-bar but no mobile day-select element. The ID contract list (Technical Hints: 'ID preservation contract') does not list any mobile day-select ID.
blocking_issues.proposed_fix: Add explicit DOM to the HTML structure snippet: a <select id='mobile-day-select'> inside #pane-middle header (after .middle-tab-bar, before tab-content divs), visible only on mobile via CSS. Add to state.js wiring: populate it from state.days in renderDaysPanel() or a new renderMobileDaySelect(), wire onchange to setActiveDay(). Add to ID preservation contract. Extend AC8: 'AND the mobile day-select dropdown shows the currently active day, AND changing it re-renders Timeline and Candidates'. Add CSS: #mobile-day-select { display: none; } @media (max-width: 639px) { #mobile-day-select { display: block; } }

blocking_issues.title: AC1 does not assert active-row highlight updates on day change
blocking_issues.description: AC1 THEN clause says 'clicking any row sets that day as active and re-renders Timeline and Candidates'. It does NOT assert that the Days panel itself re-renders so the active row highlight moves. The spec's Technical Hints say to add renderDaysPanel() to renderAll(), but this is prose guidance, not an AC assertion. A dev could: (a) call renderDaysPanel() from init() but NOT from renderAll(), causing the highlight to never update; (b) pass AC1 because Timeline and Candidates do re-render; and (c) pass AC11 because no null crash occurs. The user requirement R1 explicitly requires 'selected day highlighted with 3px left-border' — this is a core visual feature with no verifiable AC.
blocking_issues.evidence: AC1 THEN clause verbatim: 'clicking any row sets that day as active and re-renders Timeline and Candidates'. No mention of Days panel re-render. R1 acceptance_criterion in requirements_decomposition: 'active day has accent left-border'. The Technical Hints M5 section says 'Add renderDaysPanel() to renderAll()' but this is guidance, not an AC. The renderAll() function (state.js:128-136) currently calls _renderDayPickerOptions() which must be replaced — if dev forgets to add renderDaysPanel(), all existing ACs still pass.
blocking_issues.proposed_fix: Extend AC1 THEN clause: 'AND after clicking Day N row, the Day N row has the day-row--active class and 3px left-border accent, AND the previously active row no longer has the active class'. This makes the re-render of the Days panel itself a verifiable acceptance criterion.
blocking_issues.note: Codex classifies this as MAJOR (not blocking dev) since spec prose already instructs renderDaysPanel() in renderAll(). It does block QA close because the AC is insufficient to verify R1. BA must add the AC extension before dev begins to avoid a QA iteration.

major_issues.title: AF-01 typography hierarchy (M10) has no verifiable acceptance criterion
major_issues.description: M10 specifies h2=20px/600, h3=16px/600, body=14px/400, caption=12px. The spec explicitly states AF-01 is 'unresolved' and is addressed by this cycle. However none of AC1-AC11 verify any computed font-size or font-weight for content headings. The CSS M9/M10 spec lists the changes but no AC requires QA to verify h2/h3 computed sizes. Additionally, no specific CSS selector is given for the 20px h2 rule — a global h2 {} selector would override .pane-title (11px uppercase), which M10 itself says must remain at 11px. This means a dev could add an incorrect global h2 rule that breaks .pane-title while all ACs pass, OR skip the h2/h3 rules entirely while all ACs pass.
major_issues.evidence: M10 text: 'h2=20px/600 (pane section titles), h3=16px/600 (slot titles and card group titles), body=14px/400, caption=12px'. AC1-AC11 text: no AC references font-size or font-weight for content headings. .pane-title is h2.pane-title at css:173-180, 11px/600/uppercase.
major_issues.proposed_fix: Add AC12 with: THEN .slot-title computed font-size=12px (existing, correct), .candidate-group-title computed font-size=11px (existing, correct), AND the CSS rule for content h2 uses an explicit scoped selector (e.g. .tab-content h2, .pane-days h2) at 20px/600, NOT a global h2 rule. State explicitly: 'do NOT use bare h2 { } rule as it conflicts with .pane-title'. Alternatively accept that typography polish is observable-only and mark M10 as 'best-effort, not QA-gated' — but this must be explicit.

major_issues.title: state.js:512 pre_existing_guard code_snippet is wrong
major_issues.description: The context JSON pre_existing_guards entry for state.js:512 shows code_snippet: 'const btn = document.getElementById("approve-day-btn"); if (!day) { btn.disabled = true; return; }'. This snippet implies the null check on btn is absent. The actual code at state.js:512-522 shows: 'const btn = document.getElementById("approve-day-btn"); const day = _getActiveDay(); if (!day) { btn.disabled = true; return; }'. This is accurate — btn IS accessed before the null check on day, confirming the null-crash risk BA identified. The snippet is slightly paraphrased but the evidence is correct.
major_issues.evidence: state.js:512-522 actual code confirmed by Read tool.
major_issues.proposed_fix: No fix needed — BA's conclusion (null crash risk) is correct. Minor documentation inaccuracy only.

non_blocking_observations.title: M6 init() ordering is correct — Codex-corrected

So calling _activateMiddleTab('timeline') from _wireGlobalControls() fires BEFORE renderAll(), which is correct. This is NOT an issue.

non_blocking_observations.title: AC8 show/hide mechanism phrasing is behavior-correct but mechanism-ambiguous
non_blocking_observations.description: AC8 says 'clicking Candidates shows pane-candidates and hides pane-middle'. The actual mechanism uses data-mobile-hidden CSS attribute. The AC is testing user-visible behavior (correct) but QA verification needs to check data-mobile-hidden not display:none directly. This is a minor verification-recipe ambiguity, not a blocking issue.
